rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Test a substantial temperature change while keeping the gradient fixed to probe selectivity in the crowded middle cluster and late pair. All peaks currently elute well before 10 minutes, leaving time available for later gradient refinement.

Complete the temperature scout at the low-temperature boundary to test whether cooler conditions separate the persistent middle cluster. Keeping the gradient fixed isolates temperature-driven selectivity changes.

Keep the best temperature and reduce the gradient slope to improve the two unresolved pairs. The current 6.34-minute last peak leaves room to gain resolution while targeting complete elution within 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction while keeping the endpoint and duration fixed, making the gradient shallower without extending the elution window. This targets the remaining critical pair while preserving the favorable low-temperature selectivity.

Lengthen the gradient at the higher starting organic fraction to improve the remaining critical pair. The last peak at 8.18 minutes provides room for this shallower gradient while targeting elution within 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is achieved; now test a two-minute shorter gradient to reduce elution time while retaining full resolution. This brackets the critical-pair threshold between the successful 22-minute and unresolved 18-minute gradients.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step from the fully resolved method to shorten retention while also making the gradient slightly shallower. Test whether this preserves the critical pair above R = 1.5; injection 6 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Use a shallower gradient to recover resolution at the higher starting organic fraction. This tests whether the remaining critical pair can reach R ≥ 1.5 with a last-peak time shorter than injection 6.

Test a one-step temperature increase from injection 6 to shorten retention while using its resolution margin. This isolates the local temperature effect and tests whether full resolution survives at a faster elution time.

Test whether the higher starting organic fraction restores separation of the new critical pair at 30 °C. A 24-minute gradient balances the competing middle-pair resolutions while targeting faster elution than the fully resolved 25 °C methods.
Lengthen injection 11’s gradient by one step to lift the remaining critical pair above R = 1.5. Monitor the neighboring middle pair and final pair, whose resolution margins are modest.

Return to 25 °C to protect the late-pair separation, and test a higher starting organic fraction with a substantially shallower gradient. This may preserve full resolution while shortening the elution window relative to injection 9.

Test whether moving beyond the 30 °C selectivity crossover separates the late pair again while retaining middle-cluster resolution under a shallow gradient. The maximum-score methods remain available, so this run explores a potentially faster fully resolved regime.

Continue the shallow-gradient temperature scout at 50 °C to test whether further selectivity changes open the crowded middle cluster. This also targets a shorter elution window, with the fully resolved low-temperature methods retained as fallbacks.

Test the upper temperature boundary with the shallow gradient to see whether the middle and late pairs separate beyond their apparent selectivity crossovers. This completes the high-temperature scout for a faster fully resolved method.

Test a substantially shallower gradient at the higher starting organic fraction to recover the middle-pair separation lost in injection 13. The strong final solvent limits truncation risk, while the established maximum-score methods remain the fallback.
Refine the successful injection 6 with a slightly steeper gradient to shorten retention. Its slope lies between injections 6 and 7, targeting full resolution just above the critical-pair threshold.

Test a moderately steeper gradient than injection 10 to separate its critical middle pair and improve the late-pair margin. The neighboring middle pair had spare resolution, so this may yield full resolution with faster elution than injection 18.

Test the steeper-gradient side of the middle-pair selectivity crossover at the higher starting organic fraction. This may restore separation in reversed elution order and produce a substantially faster fully resolved method.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to increase separation on the reversed-order side of the middle-pair crossover. Injection 20 has resolution margin in every other pair, making this a promising route to faster full resolution.

Raise the starting organic fraction one more step to shorten the fully resolved 5.17-minute elution window. Monitor the fourth–fifth and early pairs for compression while retaining injection 21 as the faster maximum-score fallback.

Back off to the fully resolved starting composition and shorten the gradient to reduce elution time. Injection 21’s minimum resolution of 1.99 provides margin to test a steeper gradient while monitoring the middle and late pairs.
Shorten the fastest fully resolved method by one gradient-time step. This tests whether the fourth–fifth and sixth–seventh pairs retain R ≥ 1.5 while reducing the last-peak time below 4.31 minutes.

Reduce the endpoint one step to give a slope between injections 23 and 24, targeting recovery of the sole unresolved pair. This should shorten elution relative to injection 23 while aiming to retain the maximum CRF of 1.000.
